references.text: The earlier introduction to the guilt offering laws, which Leviticus 7:1 continues to elaborate on with further details about how the guilt offering is to be handled.
The sin offering is also described as 'most holy' (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים), the same designation used for the guilt offering in 7:1.
Parallel phrasing 'This is the law of the sin offering' (זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַחַטָּאת) with the same literary structure as 7:1.
Reiterates that the guilt offering is most holy and specifies who may eat it and where.
Practical application of the guilt offering in connection with the cleansing of a leper, where the guilt offering is described as most holy.
Describes the priests' share of the most holy offerings, including the guilt offering.
Ezekiel's temple vision mentions the guilt offering that is to be sacrificed at the tables in the future temple.
Ezekiel describes where the priests are to eat the most holy offerings, including the guilt offering.
